versions.html:
Training

Spend experience on the skills your character needs.

Training may apply immediately or require confirmation, depending on the training option.

Check attributes, skills and abilities, then assign usable spells to the spell slots.

Controls depend on your keyboard, gamepad and camera settings. The in-game guide shows your current bindings.

Classic edition reference

These original pages describe classic mouse and keyboard controls. Use the guidance above for current settings and gamepad controls.

Skills and abilities

This screen gives certain information about your characters, including their skills and abilities. Each character gains a certain amount of experience in the course of completing quests. Here you can 'spend' that experience to acquire new abilities and develop existing skills. You can also issue spells to characters here, which they can cast during the game.

You can select which character you're working on by using the buttons on either side of his/her name.
There are four panels in the middle of the screen. These are, from left to right:
Attributes panel
Skills and known abilities panel
Available abilities panel
Descriptions panel
See the next tutorial screens for more information on these panels.

At the bottom of the Attributes panel there's the "Your Experience" section (framed). Use the "V" and "X" buttons to confirm/cancel any changes in skills and abilities you've made using the other panels.

Note: the changes you make in other panels do not become active until you confirm them in the "Your Experience" section. If you proceed without confirming, the changes will be cancelled as soon as you switch to another screen.

Attributes

The Attributes panel shows a character's basic attributes (framed). These are : "Strength", "Dexterity" and "Intelligence", and their derivatives: "Health", "Stamina", "Actions" and "Encumbrance". The panel also shows the "Experience" the character has gained.

To learn more about each attribute, place the cursor over it and read the text which appears in the Descriptions panel.
"Experience" shows the total amount of experience your character has built up during the game. Part of that experience has already been invested in his skills and abilities (i.e. it's spent). You can use the remaining experience to develop the character's skills even further and to acquire new abilities. The amount at your disposal is shown in the "Your Experience" section.

You can invest available experience into skills and abilities using the appropriate panels. The "Your Experience" section will show the amount of experience you are spending. To confirm, click the "V" button, to cancel click "X".

Skills

At the top of the Skills and Abilities panel you can see the "Skills" section (framed). The first number after the skill's name is its current value, the second number is the price of increasing it by one unit.

To learn more about each skill, place the cursor over it and read the text which appears in the Descriptions panel.

To increase a skill click on the corresponding button.
To confirm or cancel your changes, click on the appropriate buttons in the "Your Experience" section.

Available abilities

The Available Abilities panel (framed) shows a list of abilities your character can learn. The number next to the ability name is the cost of learning this ability. If the price is dimmed it means you lack the required experience to do so.
To learn more about an ability, place the cursor over it and read the text that appears in the Descriptions panel.

To give your character an ability, click on the button with its price in the "Available Abilities" section.
To confirm or cancel, click on the appropriate buttons in the "Your Experience" section.

Note: each ability you learn significantly increases the price of learning other abilities. This means your character will not be able to learn all available abilities. A key to success in the game is selecting the right abilities.

Known abilities

At the bottom of the Skills and Abilities panel is the "Known Abilities" section (framed). You should see a number to the right of the ability name. This is what it will cost you to develop the ability one level higher
To learn more about an ability, place the cursor over it and read the text which appears in the Descriptions panel.

To develop an ability, click on the appropriate icon in the "Known Abilities" section.
To confirm or cancel, click on the appropriate buttons in the "Your Experience" section.

Note: each time you develop an ability, you increase the cost of developing other abilities.

Spells

The bar at the top of the screen shows which spells are available to your character during quests. The bar at the bottom shows your inventory.

Your inventory contains some ready-made spells. To hand one of these spells over to your character, click on its icon in the bottom bar.
To take a spell from your character and return it to your inventory click on the spell's icon in the top bar.

Note: if a spell is too complex for your character's knowledge of this particular school of magic (Elemental Magic, Sensory Magic, Astral Magic) the spell will be dimmed and you will be unable to hand it to your character. The same applies when your character cannot use a spell because he lacks the stamina to do so.
